newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Bolger committed to Employment Contracts Act.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Bolger committed to Employment Contracts Act.

text.p: New Zealand Prime Minister Jim Bolger on Tuesday said National was committed to the Employment Contracts Act and would not dump it in order to reach agreement with any future coalition partners.
On the campaign trail on Monday, Bolger said that while still committed to the ECA, National would be prepared to discuss it with likely political partners.

New Zealanders will go to the polls on October 12 for the country's first election under the new Mixed Member Proportional (MMP) system, which is likely to to produce a minority or coalition government.
Speaking on Radio New Zealand this morning, Bolger said that in the new MMP environment "the old absolutes are not quite as absolute".
"We certainly stand by the Employment Contracts Act," he said. "If someone was coming to us and said you've got to tear up the ECA, the answer would be 'no'.
But he said that did not mean that the act could not be modified or altered slightly to improve it.

"The simple reality is that people will bring items to the negotiating table, many of which will not be accommodated in the general discussions that will follow, but there may be some that you can accommodate," Bolger said.

Council of Trade Unions secretary Angela Foulkes on Monday slammed Bolger's original remarks about the ECA as a "cynical attempt by Mr Bolger to defuse the strong public opposition to the Contracts Act".

New Zealand First Party leader Winston Peters, asked if he could enter into negotiations with National on the Employment Contracts Act, told RNZ: "No. We say that the Employment Contracts Act is unstable for New Zealand and business because it can't last the way it is.
"We've asked for neutrality and fairness. I'm actually campaigning on a policy that the National Party can't disagree with because it was theirs before they betrayed the people of this country."
